generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, self-regulation is both a subject you study and a skill you use. The self-regulating learner watches how a strategy is going and amends it when the results fall short, which is exactly the monitoring loop the discipline describes. Treating a stalled revision method or a failing data-analysis approach as information, rather than a reason to work longer, is where creativity enters your own study.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two psychology students realise, three weeks into a research-methods module, that their usual way of preparing is not working.

Tom notices the method is yielding little but keeps going, reasoning that more hours will fix it. The strategy is never questioned, only intensified. By the assessment, Tom is exhausted and no further forward, having monitored the symptom without amending the cause.

Amara treats the stall as information. The monitoring says the current method is not working, so Amara asks what, specifically, it is failing to do, that is, building no intuition for the statistics, and devises a different approach aimed at that gap, working problems by hand before the software. The new strategy is given a fair trial and reviewed in turn. The problem is solved creatively, from within Amara's own regulation.

Both students saw the same warning sign. Only Amara answered it by amending the strategy rather than merely repeating it.
generatedProse.summary: Self-regulated learning in psychology becomes creative at the moment of amendment: when honest monitoring shows a method has stalled and you devise a better route rather than simply trying harder. You can now place strategy-switching in the cycle, appraise when a method is failing, and devise an alternative in your own study. The final lesson turns to creativity in psychological scholarship itself.

check.body: A study method you rely on in psychology has clearly stopped working. Which response best shows creative self-regulation?

items.text: Work out what the method is failing to do, then devise a different approach aimed at that gap.
Put in more hours on the same method until it pays off.
Switch to a module where the method is not needed.
Keep the method because it has worked in psychology before.

feedback.correct: That's right. In psychology, you diagnose what the method is failing to do and devise a better route.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for the option that changes the strategy in response to the stall.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Creative self-regulation diagnoses the gap and devises a different approach. More hours, avoidance or loyalty to the old method do not.
